title: Test scheduler access as the intended identity
goal: Explain allow-file precedence, deny-file fallback and separate PAM/account restrictions.
challenge: Begin with the documented absent allow file and root:daemon0640 deny file. Make a reversible allow fixture admitting learner and ll-at-allow but not ll-at-deny; prove specific admission/denial and owned cancellation without altering passwords/PAM/sudo/accounts. Restore exact original policy; do not claim queue admission alone proves execution. Demonstrate a real finite successful job as ll-at-allow, retain its UID/cwd/status/owned bytes and remove only its exact completed workspace. Queue admission is not completion.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/foundation-at-access.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && umask 077; here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/foundation-at-access.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700; }; fresh() { here && test "${1%/*}" = "$w" && test ! -e "$1" && test ! -L "$1"; }; regular() { here && test "${1%/*}" = "$w" && test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a:%h "$1")" = learner:600:1; }; jobid() { regular "$1" || return 19; job=$(awk '$1=="job" && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ {print $2}' "$1"); case "$job" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 19;; *) test "$job" -gt 0;; esac; }; here && test "$(df -B1 --output=avail / | tail -1)" -ge 1073741824 && systemctl is-active atd && pwd
steps.explanation: Record the private path/definitions. Refuse collisions and insufficient space; Resume reuses the recorded workspace, not a new job.
steps.expected: Owned700 workspace, actual atd and observed1GiB reserve.

steps.command: foundation_step() { here && fresh "$w/policy-before.sha" && test ! -e /etc/at.allow && test ! -L /etc/at.allow && test -f /etc/at.deny && test ! -L /etc/at.deny && test "$(stat -c %U:%G:%a:%h /etc/at.deny)" = root:daemon:640:1 || return 19; rw=$(sudo mktemp -d /var/tmp/ll-at-policy.XXXXXX) || return 19; case "$rw" in /var/tmp/ll-at-policy.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; sudo cp -p /etc/at.deny "$rw/deny.before" && sudo sha256sum /etc/passwd /etc/shadow /etc/group /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d/learning-lab /etc/at.deny > policy-before.sha && printf "Root snapshot=%s\n" "$rw" && sudo passwd -S ll-at-allow && sudo passwd -S ll-at-deny && getent passwd ll-at-allow ll-at-deny; }; foundation_step
steps.explanation: These pre-created identities have locked passwords and nologin shells. Root-authorized runuser can test scheduler policy without changing either restriction.
steps.expected: Original policy/auth hashes and protected root snapshot.

steps.command: here && fresh "$w/allow-fixture.sha" && test ! -e /etc/at.allow && test ! -L /etc/at.allow && printf "learner\nll-at-allow\n" | sudo tee /etc/at.allow >/dev/null && sudo chown root:root /etc/at.allow && sudo chmod 0644 /etc/at.allow && sha256sum /etc/at.allow > allow-fixture.sha
steps.explanation: Create only the declared allow list. Its presence takes precedence over deny; inspect actual admission as the intended identity, not root.
steps.expected: Learner and ll-at-allow listed, ll-at-deny not listed.

steps.command: foundation_step() { here && fresh "$w/denied.txt" || return 19; if printf '/usr/bin/true\n' | sudo /usr/sbin/runuser -u ll-at-deny -- /usr/bin/at -M now + 2 minutes > denied.txt 2>&1; then return 1; else test $? = 1 && grep -F "do not have permission" denied.txt; fi; }; foundation_step
steps.explanation: Specific queue-policy refusal is separate from password locking, account expiry or interactive-shell restriction. Do not change PAM/passwords to make it pass.

steps.command: foundation_step() { here && fresh "$w/allowed.log" && fresh "$w/allow-queue.txt" && fresh "$w/wrong-owner.txt" && fresh "$w/allow-after.txt" || return 19; printf '/usr/bin/true\n' | sudo /usr/sbin/runuser -u ll-at-allow -- /usr/bin/at -M now + 2 minutes > allowed.log 2>&1 && jobid "$w/allowed.log" && sudo /usr/sbin/runuser -u ll-at-allow -- /usr/bin/atq > allow-queue.txt && awk -v id="$job" '$1==id && $NF=="ll-at-allow" {f=1} END {exit !f}' allow-queue.txt || return 19; if atrm "$job" > wrong-owner.txt 2>&1; then return 1; else test $? -ne 0 || return 19; fi; sudo /usr/sbin/runuser -u ll-at-allow -- /usr/bin/atrm "$job" && sudo /usr/sbin/runuser -u ll-at-allow -- /usr/bin/atq > allow-after.txt && ! awk -v id="$job" '$1==id {f=1} END {exit !f}' allow-after.txt; }; foundation_step
steps.explanation: Capture actual ownership, prove learner cannot cancel the other identity’s job, then cancel exactly as its owner. Admission/cancellation does not alone prove execution; the companion execution lesson and developer feasibility record demonstrate that separately.
steps.expected: Owned cancellation and explicit wrong-owner refusal.

steps.command:
foundation_step() { here && fresh "$w/access-job.sh" || return 19; aw=$(sudo mktemp -d /var/tmp/ll-at-job.XXXXXX) || return 19; case "$aw" in /var/tmp/ll-at-job.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; sudo chown ll-at-allow:ll-at-allow "$aw" && test "$(stat -c %U:%G:%a "$aw")" = ll-at-allow:ll-at-allow:700 || return 19; cat > access-job.sh <<'LL_ACCESS'
#!/bin/sh
umask 077 || exit 90
ulimit -f 8 || exit 91
test ! -e result && test ! -L result || exit 89
set -C || exit 92
{ /usr/bin/timeout --kill-after=2s 6s /bin/sh -c 'test "$(id -un)" = ll-at-allow && printf "identity=%s\nuid=%s\ncwd=%s\numask=%s\n" "$(id -un)" "$(id -u)" "$(pwd -P)" "$(umask)" && printf "bounded-access-job\n"'; rc=$?; printf 'exit=%s\n' "$rc"; } > result 2>&1
exit "$rc"
LL_ACCESS
creation_rc=$?; test "$creation_rc" = 0 || return 19;
regular "$w/access-job.sh" && sudo install -o ll-at-allow -g ll-at-allow -m 0600 access-job.sh "$aw/job.sh" && fresh "$w/access-queued.log" && sudo test ! -e "$aw/result" && sudo test ! -L "$aw/result" && sudo /usr/sbin/runuser -u ll-at-allow -- /bin/sh -c 'cd "$1" && exec /usr/bin/at -M -f "$1/job.sh" now + 1 minute' sh "$aw" > access-queued.log 2>&1 && jobid "$w/access-queued.log" && printf "Recorded owned workspace=%s job=%s\n" "$aw" "$job"; }; foundation_step
steps.explanation: Admission alone is not execution. Submit one bounded job from its accessible owner-matched workspace via root-authorized runuser, not by changing its login/password restrictions.
steps.expected: Finite owned job and recorded unique path/ID.

steps.command: foundation_step() { here && jobid "$w/access-queued.log" || return 19; case "$aw" in /var/tmp/ll-at-job.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "$(sudo realpath -e "$aw")" = "$aw" && test "$(stat -c %U:%G:%a "$aw")" = ll-at-allow:ll-at-allow:700 || return 19; deadline=$(( $(date +%s)+150 )); while ! sudo grep -Fxq exit=0 "$aw/result" 2>/dev/null; do test "$(date +%s)" -lt "$deadline" || return 19; sleep 1; done; sudo test -f "$aw/result" && sudo test ! -L "$aw/result" && test "$(sudo stat -c %U:%G:%a:%h "$aw/result")" = ll-at-allow:ll-at-allow:600:1 && test "$(sudo stat -c %s "$aw/result")" -le 4096 && sudo grep -Fx identity=ll-at-allow "$aw/result" && sudo grep -Fx "uid=$(id -u ll-at-allow)" "$aw/result" && sudo grep -Fx "cwd=$aw" "$aw/result" && sudo grep -Fx umask=0077 "$aw/result" && fresh "$w/access-result.txt" && sudo cat "$aw/result" > access-result.txt || return 19; while :; do fresh "$w/access-queue-current.txt" || regular "$w/access-queue-current.txt" || return 19; sudo /usr/sbin/runuser -u ll-at-allow -- atq > access-queue-current.txt || return 19; if awk -v id="$job" '$1==id {f=1} END {exit !f}' access-queue-current.txt; then test "$(date +%s)" -lt "$deadline" || return 19; sleep 1; else break; fi; done; }; foundation_step
steps.explanation: Verify actual successful execution as the locked disposable identity, output/status/UID/cwd/umask and owner-query departure.
steps.expected: Actual ll-at-allow execution, not root output or admission-only proof.

steps.command: here && sha256sum -c allow-fixture.sha && sudo test -f "$rw/deny.before" && sudo test ! -L "$rw/deny.before" && test "$(sudo stat -c %U:%G:%a:%h "$rw/deny.before")" = root:daemon:640:1 && sudo cmp /etc/at.deny "$rw/deny.before" && test "$(stat -c %U:%G:%a:%h /etc/at.allow)" = root:root:644:1 && sudo rm -- /etc/at.allow && sudo sha256sum -c policy-before.sha && test ! -e /etc/at.allow && test ! -L /etc/at.allow
steps.explanation: Restore exact policy by removing only the known byte-matched allow fixture. Keep original deny and identities; no account deletion, shadow or sudo edit.
steps.expected: Original auth/sudo/deny bytes unchanged; allow absent again.

steps.command: foundation_step() { here && regular "$w/access-result.txt" || return 19; case "$aw" in /var/tmp/ll-at-job.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "$(sudo realpath -e "$aw")" = "$aw" && test "$(stat -c %U:%G:%a "$aw")" = ll-at-allow:ll-at-allow:700 && sudo test -f "$aw/job.sh" && sudo test ! -L "$aw/job.sh" && test "$(sudo stat -c %U:%G:%a:%h "$aw/job.sh")" = ll-at-allow:ll-at-allow:600:1 && sudo cmp "$w/access-job.sh" "$aw/job.sh" && sudo cmp "$w/access-result.txt" "$aw/result" || return 19; sudo rm -- "$aw/job.sh" "$aw/result" && sudo rmdir -- "$aw"; }; foundation_step
steps.explanation: After successful departure and policy rollback, compare retained script/result then remove only these exact owned files and empty directory. Unknown members cause rmdir refusal; no recursive removal.
steps.expected: Owned output retained in learner workspace, exact temporary owner workspace removed.

hints: Root bypass is not ordinary-user permission; policy admission does not prove PAM/account execution success; never enable passwords to make a test pass.
Use the actual dynamically captured job ID and successful owner-matched queue queries; a command failure is not an empty queue.
Inspect actual result ownership, bytes and exit status; cancel only positively matched pending work before exact rollback.
review: I demonstrated the selected mode’s facts, actual identities/results and an incorrect interpretation or attempt.
I can separate queueing, execution, access policy and self-reviewed reasoning. Completion is unscored and not automatic verification.
I removed only positively matched owned jobs, restored any exact policy fixture and retained evidence; no authentication or host changes.
coverage: LPIC-1 active v5.0 partial 108.2 at access controls. No full objective, automatic assessment or endorsement. The plan’s 107.2 at tags were corrected to active108.2;107.2 concerns display/X11.
